info.title: Lucid API — baton-lucidchart connector surface
info.summary: The subset of Lucid's REST, OAuth2 and SCIM 2.0 APIs that baton-lucidchart calls.
info.description:
This document describes **only** the endpoints `baton-lucidchart` issues requests to, and **only** the fields its Go types declare. It is not a description of Lucid's whole API.

Scope is proven by `pkg/connector/client/*.go` (which endpoints and which fields the connector depends on); shapes, enums and status codes are proven by Lucid's published reference pages. Per-operation provenance is recorded in `x-client-location`, `x-source` and `x-accessed`, and summarised in `specs/PROVENANCE.md`.

Two hosts are covered and they are not interchangeable:

- the REST API (`https://api.lucid.co`, overridable with `--base-url`), and
- the SCIM 2.0 surface (`https://users.lucid.app/scim/v2`, overridable with `--scim-base-url`).

SCIM path items carry their own `servers` override; everything else uses the REST server.

**Paths are written as the client constructs them**, not as Lucid's reference pages render them. Lucid versions the REST API with the `Lucid-Api-Version: 1` request header (`reference-rest`), and most reference pages nonetheless display a `/v1` path prefix. The connector sends the header on every REST request and uses unversioned paths everywhere except `GET /v1/users/{userId}` and `POST /v1/transferUserContent`. That inconsistency is the connector's, and it is reproduced here deliberately so this file describes the requests that actually go on the wire. See `specs/PROVENANCE.md` for the full note.

**Pagination** is Link-header based and has no OpenAPI representation beyond the request parameter and the response header: the connector sends an opaque `pageToken` query parameter and reads the next one out of the `Link` response header (`rel="next"`, `pageToken` query value), terminating when no `Link` header is present. Both halves are modelled — `pageToken` as a parameter and `Link` as a response header — but the cursor relationship between them is not expressible and is documented in prose only.

servers.description: Lucid REST API. Default; overridable with --base-url (used by cmd/test-server). The FedRAMP/GovSuite host is https://api.lucidgov.app (client.LucidchartApiFedRampUrl).

tags.description: REST user read and account provisioning.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for an access token
post.description:
Issued by `golang.org/x/oauth2` on behalf of the connector, not by the client layer — the token source is built in `pkg/connector/connector.go` and the token URL is derived from `--base-url` so a mock server receives the grant too.

**Divergence from the published contract.** Lucid documents this endpoint at `POST /v1/oauth2/token` with an `application/json` body (`reference/createorrefreshaccesstoken`). `golang.org/x/oauth2` sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` to the unversioned `/oauth2/token`, and may send the client credentials via HTTP Basic auth instead of body fields. This document records what the connector sends; see `specs/PROVENANCE.md`.

Only the four response fields `oauth2.Token` consumes are modelled. Lucid documents more (`expires`, `client_id`, `scopes`, `user_id`, `account_id`); the connector never reads them.
post.x-evidence: docs + fixture (cmd/test-server/main.go:555); request encoding from golang.org/x/oauth2, not from the docs

400.description: Bad Request. Missing or unsupported `grant_type`, or missing credentials. Body shape is the OAuth2 error object, not Lucid's REST error envelope; not modelled because Lucid does not publish it.

get.description: Paginated. The connector sends `pageToken` only — never `pageSize` — so Lucid's 200-record default applies (`reference-rest`). The response is a bare JSON array, not an envelope; the next cursor arrives in the `Link` header.

200.description: OK. A page of User resources.

post.summary: Create a user on the account
post.description: Backs the connector's `CreateAccount` capability. Lucid documents this endpoint at `POST /v1/users`; the connector posts to the unversioned `/users` with the `Lucid-Api-Version: 1` header.

400.description: Bad Request. An input field is invalid or a required field is missing.

403.description: Forbidden. The app lacks permission to create users on the account.

409.description: Conflict. A user with the same email or username already exists. The connector maps this to `codes.AlreadyExists` (client.IsConflictError).

get.summary: Get one user by REST user ID
get.description:
Called before `transferUserContent` to resolve a user's email address, which that endpoint requires instead of an ID (CXH-1488).

Lucid returns **403, not 404**, for a user that does not exist: "if the user does not belong to the authenticated account or if the user does not exist". The connector therefore cannot treat 403 as "gone" and disambiguates through SCIM `GET /Users/{id}` instead (see `client.IsPermissionDeniedError`, `pkg/connector/client/helpers.go:19`).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: ID of the user to be retrieved. Documented as a number; the connector formats it from a string.

403.description: Forbidden. The user does not belong to the authenticated account **or does not exist** — the two cases are indistinguishable here.

post.summary: Transfer all documents owned by one user to another
post.description:
The precondition for deleting a user whose content must be retained. Both fields are **email addresses**, not user IDs — passing an ID yields 400 (this was CXH-1488).

Rate limited to 30 requests per 5 seconds per account; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

204.description: No Content. The transfer succeeded. No response body.

400.description: Bad Request. `fromUser` and `toUser` name the same user.

403.description: Forbidden. One of the users does not exist or is not on the authenticated account.

429.description: Too Many Requests. 30 requests per 5 seconds per account. Carries `Retry-After` in seconds.

get.summary: List the contents of the account root folder
get.description:
The entry point of the folder/document sync tree. Lucid also reaches this through `GET /folders/{id}/contents` with the literal `id=root`; the connector holds it as a separate path constant (`RootFolderContentPath`) and it is modelled as a separate path here for that reason.

Paginated; the connector sends `pageToken` only.

200.description: OK. A page of FolderContent resources.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the folder, or the folder is deleted or does not exist.

get.summary: List the contents of a folder
get.description: Walked recursively during sync to discover child folders and documents. Paginated; the connector sends `pageToken` only.

200.description: OK. A page of FolderContent resources.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the folder, or the folder is deleted or does not exist.

get.summary: List all user collaborators on a folder
get.description:
Source of the folder `has-user-access:<role>` grants. Paginated; the connector sends `pageToken` only.

`userId` here becomes the grant principal's resource ID and `role` selects the entitlement; `created` is carried into grant metadata. Those are the parity-critical fields.

200.description: OK. A page of FolderUserCollaborator resources.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the folder, or the folder is deleted or does not exist.

get.summary: Get one user's collaborator role on a folder
get.description:
The read-before-write pre-check in `folderBuilder.Grant`. Sent with `uhttp.WithNoCache()` so the role it compares against is current — uhttp's GET cache (1h TTL) is not invalidated by the PUT/DELETE on this same path.

**Direct-only.** Lucid publishes it: "A user having access to a folder through one of the folder's ancestors will not be shown through this API." A role returned here is therefore always a direct share, which is what makes the Grant no-op short-circuit safe. A user with inherited-only access 404s.

200.description: OK. The FolderUserCollaborator record for this direct share.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the folder, or the folder is deleted or does not exist.

404.description: Not Found. The user is not a **direct** collaborator on the folder. Mapped to `codes.NotFound`; the caller treats this read as best-effort and falls through to the upsert.

put.summary: Create or update a user's collaborator role on a folder
put.description:
Backs `folderBuilder.Grant`. Lucid answers 200 when it updates an existing record and 201 when it creates one; the connector does not distinguish them.

The undocumented 409 below is load-bearing for grant idempotency (CXH-2285) — see its description.
put.x-evidence: docs + fixture (pkg/connector/collaborator_test.go:156); the 409 is client/fixture evidence only

200.description: OK. An existing collaborator record was updated.

201.description: Created. A new collaborator record was created.

400.description: Bad Request. Raised when the requested role is `owner` — collaborators cannot be given that role.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the folder, or the folder is deleted or does not exist.

409.description: Conflict. **Not documented by Lucid** — recorded here because the connector handles it (CXH-2285) and the test suite injects it. The body may carry the conflicting FolderUserCollaborator record, which `Grant` decodes before the status check: a 409 is an idempotent `GrantAlreadyExists` only when the conflicting record's role matches what was requested (or the record carries no role and the pre-check did not already confirm the user holds no share), and is surfaced as an error otherwise.

delete.summary: Remove a user's collaborator role from a folder
delete.description: Backs `folderBuilder.Revoke`. A 404 is treated as success (`GrantAlreadyRevoked`), not an error.

204.description: No Content. The collaborator was removed. No response body.

400.description: Bad Request. Removing the user would leave a project folder without an owner.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the folder, the folder is deleted or does not exist, or the target is the folder owner.

404.description: Not Found. The user is not a direct collaborator. Mapped to `codes.NotFound`; `Revoke` reports this as already revoked.

get.summary: List all user collaborators on a document
get.description:
Source of the document `has-user-access:<role>` grants. Paginated; the connector sends `pageToken` only.

`userId` becomes the grant principal's resource ID, `role` selects the entitlement, `created` is carried into grant metadata.

200.description: OK. A page of DocumentUserCollaborator resources.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the document, or the document is deleted or does not exist.

get.summary: Get one user's collaborator role on a document
get.description:
The read-before-write pre-check in `documentBuilder.Grant`. Sent with `uhttp.WithNoCache()` for the same reason as the folder equivalent.

**Direct-only, but not on Lucid's word.** Lucid publishes the ancestor-access caveat for folders and says nothing about it here. The behaviour was verified empirically against a live tenant under CXH-2285: a user shared only on the parent folder stays 404 at this endpoint and does not appear in `listDocumentUserCollaborators`. That is what makes the Grant no-op short-circuit safe. If Lucid ever starts reporting inherited access here, this assumption breaks.
get.x-evidence: docs + fixture (cmd/test-server/main.go:849, pkg/connector/collaborator_test.go:137); the direct-only property is observed, not documented

200.description: OK. The DocumentUserCollaborator record for this direct share.

403.description: Forbidden. The app lacks permission to the document, or the document is deleted or does not exist.

404.description: Not Found. The user is not a **direct** collaborator on the document (inherited parent-folder access also 404s here). Mapped to `codes.NotFound`; the caller treats this read as best-effort and falls through to the upsert.

put.summary: Create or update a user's collaborator role on a document
put.description: Backs `documentBuilder.Grant`. 200 on update, 201 on create; the connector does not distinguish them. The undocumented 409 is handled identically to the folder case.
put.x-evidence: docs + fixture (pkg/connector/collaborator_test.go:156); the 409 is client/fixture evidence only

200.description: OK. An existing collaborator record was updated.

201.description: Created. A new collaborator record was created.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the document, or the document is deleted or does not exist.

409.description: Conflict. **Not documented by Lucid** — recorded here because the connector handles it (CXH-2285) and the test suite injects it. The body may carry the conflicting DocumentUserCollaborator record; the same role-match rule as the folder upsert decides whether it is an idempotent `GrantAlreadyExists` or a surfaced error.

delete.summary: Remove a user's collaborator role from a document
delete.description: Backs `documentBuilder.Revoke`. A 404 is treated as success (`GrantAlreadyRevoked`), not an error.

204.description: No Content. The collaborator was removed. No response body.

403.description: Forbidden. The token lacks permission to the document, the document is deleted or does not exist, or the target is the document owner.

404.description: Not Found. The user is not a direct collaborator. Mapped to `codes.NotFound`; `Revoke` reports this as already revoked.

servers.description: Lucid SCIM 2.0. Default; overridable with --scim-base-url, which a FedRAMP/GovSuite tenant must set to its account-specific hostname (Lucid generates these per account and publishes no list). Shared by BOTH SCIM integrations — 'SCIM for admin management' and 'SCIM for content access' — which are told apart by the bearer token alone.

get.description:
The connector calls this only to answer "does this user still exist?" (`ScimUserExists`) — it discards the body and reads the status. SCIM 404s specifically for absence, which is what disambiguates REST's overloaded 403 on `GET /v1/users/{userId}`. A non-nil error means "unknown" and is never treated as "gone".

Always sent with the **admin-management** token.

200.description: OK. The SCIM User resource. The connector reads only the status code.

401.description: Unauthorized. The bearer token is invalid. Error body shape is not published by Lucid.

404.description: Not Found. The user does not exist. Mapped to `codes.NotFound`; reported as `exists=false`.

patch.summary: Modify a SCIM user (activate/deactivate, profile update)
patch.description:
**Two client methods share this operation**, differing only in the operations they put in the body:

- `SetUserActive` (`pkg/connector/client/scim.go:247`) — a single `replace` on `active`; backs the enable_user/disable_user actions.
- `UpdateUser` (`pkg/connector/client/user_management.go:74`) — `replace` on any of `name.givenName`, `name.familyName`, `emails`, `userName`, `roles`; Lucid has no REST modify-user endpoint, so all profile changes go through here.

Lucid documents `Content-Type: application/json` and a `schemas` value of `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User` rather than RFC 7644's `application/scim+json` and PatchOp URN. The connector follows Lucid's published form, not the RFC.

Lucid documents a 200 with the updated User body. The client additionally tolerates a bodyless 204 and a non-JSON or undecodable body, leaving its `ScimUser` zero-valued (`IsZero`) and reporting the write as applied-but-unconfirmed — the 2xx is what says Lucid applied it.

200.description: OK. The modified SCIM User resource — Lucid's confirmed post-write state, which is not necessarily what was requested.

204.description: No Content. Not documented by Lucid; handled by the client because a SCIM server is entitled to answer a PATCH this way. The write is applied but unconfirmed.

400.description: Bad Request. Syntax error in the PatchOp body.

401.description: Unauthorized. The bearer token is invalid.

404.description: Not Found. The user does not exist.

delete.description:
A hard delete. Callers transfer owned content first when it must be retained (see `transferUserContent`).

**Two client methods share this operation**, differing only in the bearer token, which is what routes the call to one integration or the other:

- `ScimDeleteUser` (`pkg/connector/client/scim.go:298`) — the admin-management token.
- `ScimDeleteUserContentAccess` (`pkg/connector/client/scim.go:310`) — the content-access token; optional, and skipped when that token is not configured.

The 409 is terminal for this connector: a user Lucid refuses to delete (account owner, default document owner) can never be deleted, so it is not retried.

204.description: No Content. The user was deleted. No response body.

400.description: Bad Request. An unexpected error prevented deletion.

401.description: Unauthorized. The bearer token is invalid.

404.description: Not Found. The user does not exist.

409.description: Conflict. The user cannot be deleted (e.g. account owner or default document owner). Mapped to `codes.AlreadyExists`; treated as terminal.

lucidApiKey.description: The Lucid REST API key (`--lucid-api-key`), sent as a bearer token. Used for every folder and document operation (`client.LucidAuthTypeApiKey`). Required grants per operation are noted on Lucid's reference pages (FolderReadonly, FolderEdit, DocumentEdit, ...).

lucidOAuth2.description: An OAuth2 access token (`client.LucidAuthTypeOAuth2`), obtained via `refreshAccessToken` or supplied by the platform token source. Used for the user read and account-provisioning operations.

lucidScimToken.description: The 'SCIM for admin management' bearer token (`--lucid-scim-token`). Requires Lucid Enterprise tier. Every SCIM operation the connector performs requires this token; without it the SCIM surface is unavailable.

lucidContentAccessScimToken.description: The 'SCIM for content access' (teams) bearer token (`--lucid-content-access-scim-token`). A separate, optional integration on the SAME base URL and SAME /Users/{id} path — only the token distinguishes it. Used for DELETE only.

PageToken.name: pageToken
PageToken.description: Opaque pagination cursor. The connector never constructs one: it reads it out of the previous response's `Link` header (`rel="next"`) and echoes it back. Omitted on the first request. The connector never sends `pageSize`, so Lucid's 200-record default applies.

FolderId.name: folderId
FolderId.description: ID of the folder. Numeric in Lucid's model; the connector carries it as a string.

DocumentId.name: documentId
DocumentId.description: ID of the document. An opaque string (UUID in Lucid's docs).

CollaboratorUserId.name: userId
CollaboratorUserId.description: ID of the user whose collaborator role is being read, set, or removed. Documented as a number; the connector carries it as a string.

ScimUserId.name: scimUserId
ScimUserId.description: SCIM resource ID. NOT the bare REST user ID: Lucid prefixes it with `lucid-`, so REST user 101 is SCIM resource `lucid-101`. The client applies the prefix internally (`scimResourceID`).

Link.description: Pagination link header. Present only when a further page exists; its absence terminates the connector's paging loop. Format: `<https://api.lucid.co/users?pageSize=200&pageToken=...>; rel="next"`. The connector parses the URL out of the first `;`-delimited part and reads its `pageToken` query value (`extractPageToken`).

User.description: Lucid's REST User model, narrowed to the fields `client.User` declares. Lucid also returns `avatar`; the connector does not read it, so it is not modelled.

accountId.description: The unique ID for the user's account.

email.description: The user's email. Used as the resource's login and email trait, and as the `fromUser` for transferUserContent.

userId.description: The unique ID for the user. This is the connector's user resource ID and ExternalId — parity-critical.

usernames.description: UNPROVEN. Declared by `client.User` and copied into the resource profile, but absent from every Lucid reference page consulted and from the test-server fixture. Retained because the connector reads it; see specs/PROVENANCE.md.

enabled.description: Whether the user can authenticate to Lucid. Decoded into a `*bool` so that an absent value is distinguishable from `false` — the connector only marks an account disabled on an explicit `false`.

roles.description: Administrative roles assigned to the user.

UserRole.description: Lucid's REST administrative role enum (kebab-case). Distinct from the SCIM role enum — Lucid publishes no crosswalk between them; the connector maintains one in `pkg/connector/users.go`.

username.description: Optional; Lucid defaults it to the email address.

password.description: Optional. Sent only when the platform supplied one; never logged.

roles.description: Optional. `account-owner` and `unknown-role` are in Lucid's enum but are not roles the connector offers at creation.

TransferContentPayload.description: Request body for transferUserContent (`client.TransferContentPayload`). Both values are EMAIL ADDRESSES, not user IDs.

fromUser.description: Email of the user whose content will be transferred.

toUser.description: Email of the user who will receive the content.

FolderContent.description: One item inside a folder — either a child folder or a document. `client.FolderContent`.

id.description: The item's ID. A NUMBER for folders and a UUID STRING for documents — Lucid's docs state both forms and the connector decodes it into an `interface{}`, normalising with `FolderContent.ID()`. This is the folder/document resource ID, so its string form is parity-critical (never render it via `%v`, which would produce scientific notation for large numeric IDs).

type.description: Which kind of item this is. The connector filters on the exact strings `folder` and `document`.

name.description: Name of the folder or document; becomes the resource display name.

isShortcut.description: Whether the item is a shortcut. When `--exclude-shortcuts` is set, the connector skips items with this true.

product.description: Which Lucid product a document belongs to. Documents only.

CollaboratorRole.description: A collaborator's access level. These five strings are the entitlement slugs the connector builds (`client.UserFolderRoles`) and the value carried in grant metadata.

CollaboratorWriteRole.description: The roles a collaborator can be ASSIGNED. `owner` is absent deliberately: Lucid documents "Collaborators cannot be given the role 'owner'" and answers 400 for it.

CollaboratorRoleRequest.description: Request body for both collaborator upserts. Built inline in `pkg/connector/client/mutate.go`.

FolderUserCollaboration.description: A user's direct collaborator record on a folder (`client.FolderUserCollaboration`).

folderId.description: ID of the folder. A NUMBER here, unlike the document equivalent.

userId.description: ID of the collaborating user. Becomes the grant principal's resource ID — parity-critical.

created.description: When the collaboration was created. Carried into grant metadata, and omitted from it when zero.

DocumentUserCollaboration.description: A user's direct collaborator record on a document (`client.DocumentUserCollaboration`).

documentId.description: ID of the document. A STRING here, unlike the folder equivalent.

userId.description: ID of the collaborating user. Becomes the grant principal's resource ID — parity-critical.

created.description: When the collaboration was created. Carried into grant metadata, and omitted from it when zero.

LucidError.description: Lucid's REST error envelope (`reference-rest`). The connector does not decode it: `uhttp` maps the HTTP status onto a gRPC code and `pkg/connector/client/helpers.go` classifies from there. The shape is recorded because the collaborator upserts decode an error body into the collaborator schema when one is present, and because the test-server reproduces it.

TokenRequest.description: Form-encoded body sent by `golang.org/x/oauth2` for the refresh_token grant. `client_id`/`client_secret` may instead be sent via HTTP Basic auth.

TokenResponse.description: Narrowed to the fields `oauth2.Token` consumes. Lucid documents more (`expires`, `client_id`, `scopes`, `user_id`, `account_id`); the connector reads none of them.

access_token.description: Bearer token for subsequent OAuth2-authenticated REST calls.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the access token, in seconds.

refresh_token.description: Issued when the `offline_access` scope was granted.

schemas.description: Lucid's PATCH example uses the core User URN here rather than RFC 7644's PatchOp URN, and the connector follows Lucid.

ScimPatchOperation.description: One operation within a PatchOp (`client.ScimPatchOperation`). The connector only ever sends `replace`.

op.description: Lucid documents `add`, `remove` and `replace`; the connector sends only `replace`.

path.description: Attribute path. The connector sends exactly these five, all bare (unfiltered) paths — Lucid publishes no filtered-path example.

value.description: The replacement value: boolean for `active`, string for the name/userName paths, array of objects for `emails` and `roles`.

ScimUser.description: SCIM 2.0 User resource, narrowed to the attributes `client.ScimUser` declares. Lucid returns more (`meta`, `groups`, `name.formatted`, enterprise extensions); the connector ignores them. Every field is optional: a 204 leaves the whole struct zero-valued.

id.description: SCIM resource ID, `lucid-`-prefixed (e.g. `lucid-1234`) — NOT the REST integer user ID.

active.description: Whether the user may authenticate. Decoded into a `*bool` so an absent value is distinguishable from `false`: the connector reports a deactivation as confirmed only on an explicit value.

ScimUserName.description: The SCIM complex `name` attribute, narrowed to what the connector reads. Lucid also returns `formatted`.

ScimUserEmail.description: One entry of the multi-valued `emails` attribute. The connector treats the entry flagged `primary` as authoritative and falls back to the first entry, since Lucid's user model holds one address.

ScimUserRole.description: One entry of the multi-valued `roles` attribute.

ScimRole.description: Lucid's SCIM role enum (PascalCase). Independent of the REST `UserRole` enum and strictly smaller: `account-owner`, `group-admin`, `organizational-group-admin` and `team-manager` have no SCIM counterpart and can only be set at account creation.
